newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil challenges Union Pacific in court.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil challenges Union Pacific in court.

text.p: Pennzoil Co has filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court in Delaware alleging that hostile bidder Union Pacific Resources Group Inc has failed to disclose earnings dilution which would result from the offer.

The oil company said that the Union Pacific offer, which comprises a stock as well as a cash offer in two parts could potentially jeopardize the tax ruling obtained from the Interal Revenue Service on the tax-free status of UPR's 1996 spin-off from Union Pacific Corporation (UPC).

"This risk results from the apparent failure to disclose to the IRS pre-spinoff discussions and contacts, direct and indirect, with Pennzoil, thereby potentially jeopardizing UPC's tax ruling relating to the UPR spin-off," Pennzoil said.
Union Pacific on Monday announced a hostile $4.0 billion bid for Pennzoil for which a second portion of 40.9 percent will be paid for by the issue Union Pacific shares.
Union Pacific said that it had been in talks with Pennzoil's management for four months but their intransigence had triggered the hostile bid.
